1. Core Clinical Tension: A hospitalized male with concurrent bacteremia presents with massive, excruciating, exophytic 12 x 15 cm crusted lesions on his hands causing complete loss of functional mobility, raising the differential between giant verrucous carcinoma, mycobacterial/fungal infection, and severe ectoparasitic infestation.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Inpatient plastic surgical consultation and examination of the hands during admission for bacteremia, prior to tangential excisional debridement and pathology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Invasive verrucous carcinoma presents with malignant epithelial fronds; deep fungal infections present with suppurative granulomas; crusted scabies manifests with hyperkeratotic stratum corneum packed with thousands of Sarcoptes scabiei mites.
case_prompt:
A male patient was admitted to the inpatient ward for systemic bacteremia, and a plastic surgery consultation was requested to evaluate severe, progressive hand lesions. The cutaneous condition had worsened over a three-year interval following an initial evaluation, during which he had been lost to specialty follow-up.

Physical examination revealed massive, exophytic, hyperkeratotic growths extensively involving both hands. The lesions were intensely painful, and the anatomical distortion and extensive tissue growth were so severe that both hands were essentially nonfunctional. Due to the severity of the lesions and functional impairment, urgent surgical intervention was indicated.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Giant Verrucous Carcinoma / Invasive Squamous Cell Carcinoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The massive, progressive 12 × 15 cm tissue proliferation causing structural destruction and loss of hand function closely mimicked a malignant verrucous neoplasm; ruled out by histopathology showing mite infestation without malignant cytology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Now, three years after his initial assessment, the involvement was so advanced that his hands were essentially nonfunctional due to pain and extensive growth, so he was scheduled for debridement

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Chronic Deep Mycobacterial or Fungal Soft-Tissue Infection
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Given the concurrent bacteremia and severe vegetative plaques, deep fungal or atypical mycobacterial infectious dermatoses were considered; ruled out by pathology confirming ectoparasitic infestation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Several months later, during in inpatient stay for bacteremia, Plastic Surgery was asked to re-evaluate the patient's hand lesions.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The patient underwent tangential excisional debridement of a 12 × 15 cm area on the right hand, with histopathological analysis demonstrating overwhelming Sarcoptes scabiei mite burden consistent with Norwegian scabies, subsequently treated with oral ivermectin and permethrin cream.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He underwent tangential right hand excisional debridement, 12 x 15 cm, for which pathology was positive for Norwegian Scabies infestation

editor_comments: Zero spoilers in admission narrative. Debridement pathology and targeted antiparasitic therapy preserved for diagnostic reasoning.
